name: Pork Tenderloin With Rhubarb Sauce

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as canola oil, divided
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
finely chopped mixed fresh tender herbs

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, combine chicken stock or broth with wine and sprinkle gelatin evenly over surface; set aside. Cut tenderloin in half crosswise and season on all sides with 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Place cornstarch in a fine-mesh strainer, and dust cornstarch over tenderloin halves, lightly coating all sides.

In a 25-cm stainless steel skillet, heat 1 1/2 tablespoons oil over high until shimmering. Add pork; cook, turning as needed, until well browned on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes total. Transfer to a large plate; set aside.

Reduce heat to low. To now-empty skillet, add shallot, garlic, and remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons oil and cook, stirring constantly, until softened and fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add chicken stock–gelatin mixture, orange marmalade, mustard, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper. Bring to a vigorous simmer over medium-high, stirring occasionally. Return pork along with any of its accumulated juices to skillet; cook, turning about every 2 minutes and adjusting heat as needed to maintain a vigorous simmer, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest portion of pork registers 120 to 54°C (49 to 54°C) for medium-rare or 130 to 60°C (54 to 60°C) for medium, 6 to 10 minutes. Transfer pork to a cutting board.

Add rhubarb and butter to sauce in skillet and continue to vigorously simmer over medium-low, adjusting heat as needed, until rhubarb is tender, sauce is thickened and glossy and lightly coats the back of a spoon, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from heat, and stir in herbs. Return pork to skillet, and turn to coat, then return pork to cutting board.
Slice pork thinly crosswise and serve with rhubarb sauce.

schema_metadata.keywords: Roast Pork Tenderloin with Rhubarb Sauce, skillet-roasted pork tenderloin, rhubarb dinner recipe

description: This pork tenderloin with a jammy rhubarb sauce comes together in just 30 minutes, and is perfect for any night of the week. Make it in the spring with fresh rhubarb or year-round with frozen.
notes:
Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → store-bought low-sodium chicken broth; dry white wine → dry vermouth; orange marmalade → preserves; cubed fresh rhubarb → thawed frozen rhubarb

Notes: This recipe can easily be doubled with two pork tenderloins in a 30-cm skillet.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftover cooked pork and sauce can be refrigerated separately in airtight containers for up to 4 days.
author: Leah Colins
